conversation-intelligence.title: Coach sellers with conversation intelligence
conversation-intelligence.notes: Conversation intelligence in Dynamics 365 Sales applies analytics and data science to recorded seller calls together with Dynamics 365 Sales data, so that managers can coach their teams with evidence instead of impressions. It presents key indicators per team, per seller and per call. Signals it surfaces include keywords, brands and competitors that customers mention (including trending ones), price discussions, customer sentiment, the conversational style of sellers and of top performers, and signals and action items raised during calls. Managers can listen to calls, read transcripts, translate non-English transcripts into English and define tracked keywords and competitors for their team; sellers see their own insights and call history. Administrators configure organization-wide tracked terms, data retention periods, the connection to the Dynamics 365 environment, call processing monitoring and the hierarchy levels managers may view. A manager hierarchy must be set up, Teams calls are supported in the Sales Hub and the standalone app, and a defined list of transcript languages is supported. Microsoft states the feature must not be used for decisions about employees, and customers remain responsible for notice, consent and recording laws.

power-apps-for-figma.title: Meets the Plugin - Power Plugins
power-apps-for-figma.notes: Power Apps for Figma is a Figma plugin published by Power Plugins whose help article, written by Lukas Pavelka, introduces its interface. Its purpose is to prepare Figma designs so they can be exported to Power Apps. The Editor tab manages designs before export and offers a Layout view, listing selected screens and controls that carry supported name prefixes, and a Code view showing the YAML. It includes a theme and style tool based on design tokens or saved styles and an import function that brings YAML and Base64 images into Figma. A bottom action bar offers Compile (adds prefixes automatically), a dependency model of screen navigation, PDF export, YAML export (ZIP for several screens), resizing for mobile or tablet, translation and a bulk manager for renaming layers. A Generate tab, described as alpha, is an AI chat that creates modern Power Apps controls from prompts, with custom controls planned. Further tabs cover settings, help with supported prefixes and a history that compares versions. The article distinguishes a free version from a PRO version, with extra settings and a Get PRO button for free users, though its own tab counts are inconsistent.

slide-master.title: What is a slide master in PowerPoint? - Microsoft Support
slide-master.notes: The slide master in PowerPoint is the top slide in Slide Master view, opened from the View tab. It controls the fonts, images such as logos and other elements shared by all slides built on it, so one edit updates every dependent slide. Most work is done on the layout masters that belong to it: each layout defines its own arrangement of placeholders for titles, text and objects, and every master includes a Title Slide Layout. A theme bundles coordinated colors, fonts and effects such as shadows and reflections, and each theme comes with its own slide master and set of layouts; using several themes in one presentation therefore produces several masters. Fonts and colors reach slides through the master and layouts. Microsoft advises editing masters before creating slides, because changed layouts must otherwise be reapplied to existing slides in Normal view. Elements that cannot be edited in Normal view are usually defined on the master or a layout. In Microsoft 365 for Windows, PowerPoint offers to remove unused masters once a file holds 25 or more. The article applies to PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 and the 2016 to 2024 versions.

progressive-disclosure.title: Agent Skills - Claude Platform Docs
progressive-disclosure.notes: The Claude documentation on Agent Skills uses progressive disclosure to explain how skills avoid filling the context window. A skill is a directory containing instructions, metadata and optional resources such as scripts and templates, and Claude loads it in three levels. Level 1 is the name and description from the YAML frontmatter, always present at startup at roughly 100 tokens per skill. Level 2 is the body of SKILL.md, read only when a request matches the description, and expected to stay under about 5,000 tokens. Level 3 covers bundled files, references and scripts that are opened only when needed; files never accessed cost no tokens, and for scripts only their output enters the context, not the code. Because only names and descriptions occupy context until a skill triggers, many skills can be installed without a meaningful penalty. The description is what Claude matches against the request, so it must say what the skill does and when to use it; vague descriptions make triggering unreliable. Documented limits include a name of at most 64 characters and a description of 1 to 1,024 characters.

point-of-presence.title: What is Azure Front Door? - Microsoft Learn
point-of-presence.notes: Azure Front Door is Microsoft's cloud content delivery network and application delivery service, listed alongside Azure Load Balancer and Application Gateway as a load-balancing and delivery option. It serves static and dynamic web content through global and local points of presence placed close to users. The page cites more than 118 edge locations across 100 metro areas, linked to Azure over a private enterprise-grade wide area network, and says this can improve latency by up to three times. Acceleration relies on a unicast network, where clients reach a specific edge location, and on split TCP, where the client connection ends at the nearby edge and a separate connection runs to the origin over Microsoft's backbone. Front Door also supports end-to-end IPv6 and HTTP/2, routes and load balances across origins in Azure or elsewhere, probes origin health and offers a rules engine at the edge. Security features at the edge include layer 3-4 DDoS protection, a web application firewall, bot protection, TLS offload with managed certificates and Private Link to origins. It is sold in Standard, Premium and Classic tiers.

pnpjs.title: PnP/PnPjs
pnpjs.notes: PnPjs is an open source set of client-side libraries from the Microsoft 365 and Power Platform Community (PnP). The project describes it as a collection of fluent libraries for consuming SharePoint, Graph and Office 365 REST APIs in a type-safe way. Calls are built with a chainable, fluent syntax, and typings give IntelliSense help while composing queries. It runs inside SharePoint Framework solutions, in Node.js and in ordinary JavaScript or browser projects. The code is split into packages published under the @pnp scope that depend on each other: sp for SharePoint REST, graph for Microsoft Graph, sp-admin for tenant admin methods, plus core, queryable, logging, nodejs and client wrappers for MSAL (msaljsclient) and Azure Identity (azidjsclient). The documentation covers authentication separately for SPFx, browser and Node.js, batching and caching, async paging, error handling, selective imports for smaller bundles, and behaviors that customize how requests are processed. A transition guide helps users move from version 2. Bugs and ideas are handled as GitHub issues under the Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct.

small-language-model.title: Small language model - Wikipedia
small-language-model.notes: Small language models, also called compact language models, are language models built for natural language tasks such as text generation but small enough to be trained or run on consumer hardware, including personal computers, laptops and smart devices. The article puts them typically below about 40 billion parameters, with many families under 10 billion, whereas large language models often have hundreds of billions and sometimes more than a trillion. Most SLMs use the same architecture as LLMs with fewer parameters and sometimes lower numeric precision, and they are commonly shrunk with knowledge distillation, pruning and quantization. Pre-training helps even very small models, and larger pre-training data generally improves results. Listed families include Gemma, Granite, Ministral, Phi, Qwen, SmolLM (with 135M, 360M and 1.7B variants) and Apple's on-device foundation models. Advantages are far lower compute needs and the ability to run locally without cloud access. The trade-off is that fewer parameters limit how much information a model can encode, which can reduce generalization and accuracy compared with large models and makes quality depend heavily on the match between training data and task.

en-16931.title: Compliance with eInvoicing standard - European Commission Digital Building Blocks
en-16931.notes: EN 16931 is the European standard on electronic invoicing, developed and published by CEN at the request of the European Commission. Its aim is that a seller can send invoices to many customers in one eInvoicing format instead of adapting to each buyer. Part 1 defines the semantic data model: it lists every business term allowed in a compliant invoice, explains what each term means and how it is used, and sets the business rules. The model is meant for computer-to-computer exchange, where definitions must be more precise than on a paper invoice. The standard describes what invoice content means, not how it is technically structured. The semantic model is bound to two XML syntaxes: UBL 2.1 Invoice (mapping in part 3.2) and the UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice, CII (part 3.3). The page illustrates this with the seller name, business term BT-27, which must appear exactly once and sits in different element paths in UBL and CII. Exact compliance lets buyers process invoices automatically in their accounting systems, and validation artefacts exist for design-time and run-time checks. Changes follow the CEN maintenance procedure, and CEN is working on a revision.

content-security-policy.title: Content Security Policy - Wikipedia
content-security-policy.notes: Content Security Policy (CSP) is a web security standard meant to prevent cross-site scripting, clickjacking and other code injection attacks. A server sends a Content-Security-Policy header listing which origins a browser may load scripts, styles, frames, fonts, images, media and other content from, and a compliant browser enforces that allowlist. Once a policy is enforced, inline JavaScript and inline CSS are disabled by default, as are eval() and similar dynamic code evaluation. Exceptions can be granted selectively with nonce or hash values for trusted inline code, while the unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval keywords switch the restrictions off globally. Violations can be sent as JSON reports to a reporting endpoint, and a site may combine enforcing and report-only policies. Recommended practice is to load code from external files, parse JSON instead of evaluating it and attach event handlers with addEventListener. Robert Hansen proposed the idea in 2004 under the name Content Restrictions; version 1.0 became a W3C Candidate Recommendation in 2012, Level 2 followed in 2014 and Level 3 was in development in 2023. The article also notes that attackers have published bypasses, for example via nonce or allowlist misconfiguration and vulnerable libraries on trusted CDNs.

workplace-loneliness.title: Loneliness - Wikipedia
workplace-loneliness.notes: This general article on loneliness is the closest verifiable concept page; it has no dedicated section on workplace loneliness. It describes loneliness as an unpleasant emotional response to perceived or actual social isolation and stresses that it is subjective: people can feel lonely in a crowd and content alone, and it differs from solitude. It distinguishes social loneliness (lacking a wider network or community) from emotional loneliness (lacking close, nurturing relationships), and short-term from chronic loneliness, with the latter linked to poorer health. Causes named include lack of meaningful relationships, loss, relocation, retirement, poor health, personality traits and conditions such as depression and anxiety. Effects reported include associations with cardiovascular problems, depression, sleep problems and memory or dementia risk. The article cites the WHO estimate that about one in six people worldwide experience significant long-term loneliness and notes that the WHO declared loneliness a global public health concern in 2023. It also observes that people with successful careers can still be lonely, and that therapy, social prescribing and community programs are common interventions.

copilot-vision.title: Get started with vision capabilities in Microsoft Copilot - Microsoft Support
copilot-vision.notes: Vision in Microsoft Copilot lets a user share a Windows or web desktop screen, or a mobile device camera, so Copilot can answer questions about what is visible. Copilot analyzes the shared content in real time and grounds answers in that content and, for work accounts, in work data. It works only during a voice conversation: the user starts a voice chat from the Copilot Chat input, the Copilot key, Win+C or the mobile app, then selects the screen-share arrow on desktop or the camera icon on mobile, and stops with Stop sharing. Requirements are a Microsoft Copilot license for work or school accounts, or a Microsoft 365 Personal, Family or Premium subscription for personal accounts, plus microphone access and, on mobile, camera permission. A privacy notice may appear on first use, and each vision conversation is independent, so earlier screens or camera input are not reused. Copilot does not act on the user's behalf in this mode: it may highlight parts of the screen but does not click, type or scroll. Availability, regions and languages vary while features roll out.

programmable-logic-controller.title: Programmable logic controller - Wikipedia
programmable-logic-controller.notes: A programmable logic controller (PLC) is a ruggedized industrial computer used to control manufacturing processes, machines and assembly lines, designed for reliability, ease of programming and fault diagnosis. It acts as a hard real-time system that must produce outputs within a limited time after inputs change. Its parts are a CPU, power supply, memory, I/O interface and communications interface. It repeats a scan cycle of reading inputs, executing the program and writing outputs, which typically takes tens of milliseconds. Inputs and outputs are discrete (on/off, such as limit switches) or analog (pressure, temperature; a 4-20 mA loop maps to 0 to 32,767). PLCs began in the late 1960s in the US car industry to replace hard-wired relays and sequencers; the first, the Modicon 084, followed a 1968 General Motors request. IEC 61131-3 is the main programming standard, with Structured Text, Instruction List, ladder logic, function block diagram and sequential function chart. Ladder logic remains popular because its scan-based execution is predictable. PLCs connect over Ethernet, serial ports and protocols such as Modbus, usually with HMIs and SCADA, and safety PLCs meet SIL requirements. Programs are not fully portable between vendors.

functional-governance.title: A collaboration governance framework for Microsoft 365 - Microsoft Learn
functional-governance.notes: This archived Microsoft Learn framework describes collaboration governance as managing access to resources, keeping collaboration compliant with business standards and securing data, partly to limit shadow IT. Its section on functional and organizational governance is a checklist: talk to heavy collaborators, balance risk and benefit, adapt to departments and content types, align effort to business priorities, embed decisions in settings that switch features on or off, roll out in phases while watching help desk tickets, train users, publish policies on an adoption site, define roles with a governance core team and revisit decisions regularly. First decisions should cover provisioning, naming and external access. The organization and lifecycle area asks for policies on group and team creation, naming, expiration and archiving, and for end-of-life options for groups, teams, sites and Viva Engage communities. Technical governance builds on Microsoft 365 Groups, with controls such as external sharing settings, domain allow and block lists, restricted group creation, naming policy, expiration policy and per-group guest access, mostly requiring E3 or E5 and sometimes Entra ID P1 or P2. The page is marked archived and last updated in July 2023, and it does not cover templates.

key-person-dependency.title: Bus factor - Wikipedia
key-person-dependency.notes: The bus factor, also called truck, lottery or circus factor, measures the risk that arises when knowledge and capabilities are not shared across a team. It is the smallest number of team members who would have to leave suddenly before a project stalls because nobody else has the required knowledge. The article links it to key person risk but focuses on technical experts rather than easily replaced managers or financial leaders. A person counts only if they are both key to the work and irreplaceable. In software the risk often stems from undocumented or unshared work, so a component that only one person understands is a key dependency. A bus factor of 1 is a single point of failure, while higher values mean more redundancy. The example of a 30-person bakery shows it: if only five people can bake, the factor is five. Departure need not be dramatic; a new job or parental leave has the same effect. Suggested mitigations are reducing complexity, documenting and updating processes, cross-training and sharing information. A 2015 to 2016 study of 133 popular GitHub projects found that 65 percent had a bus factor of two or less.

prompt-chaining.title: Prompting best practices - Claude Platform Docs (prompt chaining)
prompt-chaining.notes: The Claude documentation defines prompt chaining as breaking a task into sequential API calls in which each call's output feeds the next. It says that with adaptive thinking and subagent orchestration, Claude now handles most multistep reasoning internally, so explicit chaining is no longer the default way to get multistep reasoning. It remains worthwhile in two situations: when you need to inspect intermediate outputs, and when you need to enforce a specific pipeline structure. The most common pattern is self-correction in three steps: generate a draft, have the model review it against stated criteria, then refine the draft using that review. Because every step is a separate call, each can be logged, evaluated or branched on, which is described as the main practical benefit over one large prompt. Where chaining is not required, the page suggests asking the model to check its own work within a single prompt instead. The page gives only this short description and no dedicated example, and it does not discuss Microsoft 365 Copilot scenarios.

multimodal-ai.title: Multimodal learning - Wikipedia
multimodal-ai.notes: Multimodal learning is a branch of deep learning that combines and processes several kinds of data, called modalities, such as text, images, audio, video and robot proprioception. Combining them gives a fuller picture than any single type and improves tasks like visual question answering, cross-modal retrieval, text-to-image generation and image captioning. The field was proposed in 2011, and large multimodal models such as Google Gemini and GPT-4o have grown popular since 2023. Models must represent the information from each modality jointly. Approaches include early fusion, where embeddings are merged before prediction, intermediate fusion of separately processed modality representations, and cross-attention. A common recipe for multimodal LLMs converts an encoder's output into tokens that are interleaved with text tokens, often with a frozen image encoder. Examples named include CLIP for joint image-text representations, LLaVA, Whisper for audio and DALL-E for generation. Applications range from search and recommendation to healthcare diagnostics, robotics, emotion recognition and code search. Open challenges are aligning modalities, deciding how to fuse them, handling missing modalities, choosing complementary data and privacy, since combined sources can re-identify people.

entity-resolution.title: Record linkage - Wikipedia
entity-resolution.notes: Record linkage, also called data matching, entity resolution or deduplication, is the task of finding records in one or more data sources that refer to the same entity when no common identifier exists. The article traces it to Halbert Dunn in 1946, Howard Newcombe's probabilistic foundations in 1959 and the formal Fellegi-Sunter framework of 1969, which later machine learning methods built on. Data quality matters: standardizing names, dates and addresses first improves accuracy, and phonetic algorithms such as Soundex and metaphone help with spelling variation. Deterministic linkage matches on exact identifiers; probabilistic linkage gives each field a match and non-match weight and compares the summed score with an upper and a lower threshold, sending uncertain pairs to review. Blocking limits comparisons to records agreeing on certain fields, which speeds things up but can miss true matches. Further options are machine learning classifiers, human-in-the-loop review and privacy-preserving linkage using encoded values such as Bloom filters. Uses include master data management with a golden master record, data warehousing, public health registries and fraud detection.

opentofu.title: OpenTofu
opentofu.notes: OpenTofu is an infrastructure-as-code tool that its website describes as a drop-in replacement for Terraform, preserving existing workflows and configurations. It is a fork of Terraform started by Gruntwork, Spacelift, Harness, env0, Scalr and others after HashiCorp moved from an open source license to the Business Source License, which the project calls ambiguous for companies and developers. OpenTofu sits under the Linux Foundation's stewardship and is described as community driven, aiming for feature parity with Terraform; contributions come through GitHub discussions, issues, RFC reviews and code, and the site credits more than 180 community contributors plus sponsors for hosting and monitoring. The page cites an ecosystem of over 3,900 providers and 23,600 modules that manage resources across clouds, with examples for AWS S3, Cloudflare DNS and GitHub repositories. Features it highlights include the -exclude flag and provider for_each in version 1.9, early evaluation of variables and locals in module sources in 1.8, and client-side state encryption in 1.7 with key providers such as PBKDF2, AWS KMS, GCP KMS and OpenBao. A registry search site lists providers and modules. The page does not itself state OpenTofu's own license.

managing-director.title: Chief executive officer - Wikipedia (Managing director)
managing-director.notes: The Wikipedia article reached under the title Managing director treats it as another name for the chief executive officer, the top-ranking officer who manages a company or nonprofit. The CEO reports to the board of directors, leads strategy and key policy decisions, implements the targets the board sets, oversees day-to-day operations such as marketing, finance and human resources, reports on status to the board, motivates staff, drives change and communicates with press, public and employees, and is ultimately accountable for business decisions. On usage, the article says that in the United Kingdom managing director is often used in business and the charity sector instead of CEO, while charities avoid the word director for senior staff to prevent confusion with unpaid trustees. In the United States CEO is the business term and executive director is used mainly in not-for-profits, with distinct legal duties. Countries with a dual board have an executive board led by the CEO and a separate supervisory board with its own chair. The article does not mention Germany or the title Geschaeftsfuehrer. It dates the title chief executive officer to a 1782 US ordinance and the CEO acronym to Australia in 1914.

microsoft-ignite.title: Microsoft Ignite - Wikipedia
microsoft-ignite.notes: Microsoft Ignite is Microsoft's annual conference for developers, IT professionals and partners. The first event took place in 1993 in Orlando under the name TechEd, and after the 2014 TechEd in Barcelona Microsoft adopted the Ignite name from 2015. From 2024 the former partner event Microsoft Inspire was merged into Ignite, creating one event for both audiences. Editions typically run three to five days with presentations, whiteboard sessions, hands-on labs, expert and MVP access, an exhibition area and a large session catalog published in advance. The article lists North American editions: Chicago in May 2015, Atlanta in September 2016, Orlando from 2017 to 2019, digital events in 2020 and 2021, a hybrid 2022 edition in Seattle, a 2023 Seattle edition, Chicago in November 2024 and a hybrid event at Moscone Center in San Francisco in November 2025. Historical regional TechEd editions ran in Africa, Australia, India, Israel, Latin America, the Middle East, New Zealand and Europe. Since 2020 the event has increasingly offered digital or hybrid participation, and the host city changes almost every year.

it-service-management.title: IT service management - Wikipedia
it-service-management.notes: IT service management (ITSM) is the set of activities an organization performs to plan, build, deliver, run and manage IT services for its customers. Unlike technology-centred disciplines such as network or systems management, it is process-oriented, focuses on customer needs and the services delivered, and stresses continual improvement. The article names the service desk as a core function under ITIL: the single point of contact between users and IT staff that receives incident reports, handles service requests, and manages change requests, third-party arrangements and software licensing. ITIL distinguishes it from a call center or help desk, which cover only part of this scope. Routine tasks can be automated through IT process automation, and ITSM tools are often applied beyond IT, known as enterprise service management. ITIL is the most prominent framework, aimed at aligning IT with business needs. Other frameworks and standards listed include COBIT, TOGAF, eTOM, FitSM, CMMI, ASL, USM, BiSL, the Microsoft Operations Framework and the certifiable standard ISO/IEC 20000. Professional bodies include itSMF and HDI, and certifications include ITIL 4, TOGAF and COBIT.

analytics-tool.title: Business intelligence software - Wikipedia
analytics-tool.notes: Business intelligence (BI) software is application software that retrieves, analyzes, transforms and reports on data for business intelligence. It usually reads data that has already been stored, often in a data warehouse or data mart, though that is not required. The article groups the tool types as spreadsheets, reporting and querying software, online analytical processing (OLAP), digital dashboards, data mining, data warehouses, local information systems and data cleansing tools. Reporting and querying tools extract, sort, summarize and present selected data, while analytical functions such as OLAP and data mining support deeper analysis, and cloud-hosted analytics let companies process large data volumes and visualize results. Apart from spreadsheets, BI tools can be standalone applications, suites, parts of ERP systems, APIs or components of industry software, and some are sold as data warehouse appliances. Named open source examples include Apache Superset, Grafana, KNIME and JasperReports, and commercial examples include Tableau, Qlik, MicroStrategy, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, SAS and IBM Cognos. Historically, the first comprehensive systems came from IBM and Siebel between 1970 and 1990, cloud-based BI appeared after 2000 and mobile access became a focus from 2006.

identity-security-tool.title: Zero Trust as a security foundation - Microsoft Learn
identity-security-tool.notes: This Microsoft Learn overview is a concept page for protecting identities, devices, data and applications under a Zero Trust approach. Zero Trust follows the idea never trust, always verify: access is granted only after checking who is asking, which device is used, location, behavior and risk, and verification continues throughout a session. Its three principles are verify explicitly using all available signals, use least privilege access for the shortest time needed, and assume breach, which focuses controls on limiting impact and speeding detection and response. Compared with traditional perimeter models, which trusted assets inside the network, it treats every request as untrusted because modern attacks rely on identity compromise, phishing and session hijacking rather than network position. Outcomes include continuously evaluated and temporary access, tightly scoped permissions, consistent controls across on-premises, cloud, SaaS and AI workloads, and built-in detection and response. The page stresses that security is also about human behavior and processes and that responsibility is shared.

requirements-management.title: Requirements management - Wikipedia
requirements-management.notes: Requirements management is the ongoing process of documenting, analyzing, tracing and prioritizing requirements, getting stakeholders to agree on them, controlling changes and keeping stakeholders informed. A requirement is a capability the product or service must meet, and the aim is to confirm that the needs of customers and other stakeholders are understood, verified and satisfied, from the first analysis of objectives until after release. Traceability documents each requirement's life: its origin can be followed, every change is recorded, and links connect parent and child requirements, tests and requesting people, which supports reports on compliance, completeness, coverage and consistency. Change control receives and records requests, analyzes their impact, implements approved ones, checks them through quality assurance and closes them. The article walks through investigation, feasibility, design, construction and test, and release phases and names four verification methods: analysis, inspection, testing and demonstration. Some organizations use only documents, others tools with a database, traceability links, baselines and version control; the article advises adopting tools incrementally within wider process improvement.

erp-analytics-mcp.title: Dynamics 365 ERP Analytics MCP for finance and operations apps (preview) - Microsoft Learn
erp-analytics-mcp.notes: The Dynamics 365 ERP Analytics MCP server lets AI agents query Business performance analytics (BPA) data in natural language, so users need not write DAX queries or navigate report interfaces. BPA turns transactional data from Dynamics 365 finance and operations into dimensional models for record-to-report, procure-to-pay and order-to-cash. The agent interprets a question, fetches the BPA schema, generates and runs DAX and returns structured JSON insights. The server exposes two tools: get-bpa-dataset-schema, which returns tables, columns, measures and relationships, and execute-dax-query, which runs DAX with automatic row-level security. The authenticated user's security role limits what the agent can see. Prerequisites are finance and operations version 10.0.38 or higher, BPA version 2.4.3224 or higher, the Basic user role, the BPA user role and an agent platform that supports MCP. A two-tier design uses pre-transformed models refreshed about every 12 hours plus on-demand DAX, so answers reflect the last refresh rather than real time. It can be combined with the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server to move from insight to action. The feature is in preview and not meant for production, and the page lists no quotas.

copilot-ux-components.title: Overview of Copilot UX components - Microsoft Learn
copilot-ux-components.notes: Copilot UX components extend Microsoft 365 Copilot with custom interactive interfaces built with the SharePoint Framework (SPFx), so a conversation can show branded, interactive experiences instead of plain text. A solution packages one or more components with a declarative agent that makes them discoverable and callable; components derive from BaseCopilotComponent, declare tools and display modes in a manifest and render inline or fullscreen, with the host controlling layout. Tools receive parameters through a properties schema. The same shared UI can be reused in an SPFx web part or Teams tab through separate adapters. Packages are .sppkg files deployed through the SharePoint App Catalog, with assets hosted automatically when includeClientSideAssets is set, and distribution is private or through the SharePoint Store. The page says they are generally available from SPFx 1.24, released on 28 October 2026, and requires a user-specific Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license on top of E3, E5 or E7, even for development. A Copilot Workbench supports local testing. Limits include a 10 KB text context for Copilot, no mobile support, a sync mismatch when combined with Teams functionality, and no coverage of additional surfaces yet.

sharepoint-html-pages.title: Create, upload, edit, and publish HTML pages in SharePoint - Microsoft Support
sharepoint-html-pages.notes: HTML pages are SharePoint pages built from HTML content and stored in the Site Pages library like modern pages. They can be created with Copilot from a prompt, which uses the site theme and aims for accessibility, or by uploading a single .html file or a folder with its files; the HTML file may be up to 10 MB. Editing works directly on text and images or through a Copilot chat pane, and publishing makes the page visible only to people who already have permission. For security the HTML renders in a sandboxed iframe isolated from the SharePoint header and navigation, with Content Security Policy rules on top. Arbitrary fetch or outbound API calls and cross-tenant communication are blocked, JavaScript may run only if inline in the same file or from Microsoft-managed libraries such as Chart.js, Mermaid, React, Fluent UI and Babylon, and localStorage is unavailable. Links to external domains require the domain on the site's HTML Field Security allow list. Creating or editing with Copilot needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, while contributors can upload and publish without one. Site owners can disable HTML files per site, but tenant admins cannot disable them tenant-wide. Unsupported items include co-authoring, comments, mobile editing, templates and promoting to news.

a2a-protocol.title: A2A Protocol
a2a-protocol.notes: The A2A site describes Agent2Agent as an open protocol for communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications. Agents built on different platforms, such as LangGraph, CrewAI or Semantic Kernel, can connect without custom integrations for each pair, delegate sub-tasks, exchange information and coordinate actions without exposing their internal memory, tools or proprietary logic. The project is hosted by the Linux Foundation under neutral governance and an Apache 2.0 license, cites more than 170 community partners and says it has joined the Agentic AI Foundation. Extensions and custom bindings are added through a formal, tiered promotion process so the core stays stable. Six official SDKs are listed for Python, Go, Java, JavaScript, C# and .NET, and Rust, all implementing the A2A v1.0 specification. The page positions A2A as complementary to MCP: MCP connects an agent to tools, APIs and data, whereas A2A connects an agent to other agents, and it recommends using both. Its highlighted features are interoperability, complex multi-agent workflows, secure and opaque collaboration, working with MCP and extensibility. The landing page itself does not describe discovery or transport details.

active-directory-tiering.title: Enterprise access model - Microsoft Learn
active-directory-tiering.notes: This Microsoft Learn page explains the enterprise access model and how it evolved from the on-premises Active Directory tier model. The legacy tier model aimed at containing unauthorized privilege escalation in a Windows Server Active Directory environment; the page shows it only as a diagram. Its successor organizes the environment into a control plane of enterprise identity systems, a management plane for IT management infrastructure, and a data and workload plane holding applications and data, with each plane controlling those beneath it. Three access pathways cross them: user access, application access through APIs, and privileged access for administrators and developers, which must be stringently protected. The mapping from tiers is that Tier 0 becomes the control plane, widened to cover all access control including networking for legacy operational technology, Tier 1 splits into the management and data and workload planes, and Tier 2 splits into user access and app access to cover B2B, B2C and API surfaces. Required principles are Zero Trust, pervasive security and policy for all access types, and mitigating privilege escalation by enforcing hierarchy, auditing configuration weaknesses and monitoring anomalies.

adaptive-protection.title: Help dynamically mitigate risks with Adaptive Protection - Microsoft Learn
adaptive-protection.notes: Adaptive Protection in Microsoft Purview uses machine learning in Insider Risk Management to assign users a risk level and apply protection controls automatically, so low-risk users keep their productivity while high-risk users face stricter limits. It connects to Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (generally available), Data Lifecycle Management (preview, preserving content deleted by risky users for 120 days) and Microsoft Entra Conditional Access (preview). Built-in insider risk levels are Elevated, Moderate and Minor, derived from aggregated insights and alert severity, and can be customized with alert-based or activity-based conditions, a detection window of 5 to 30 days (default 7) and automatic expiration. DLP policies use the condition on the user's insider risk level and currently support only Exchange, Teams and Devices locations; Conditional Access uses an Insider risk condition and can run in report-only mode. Setup is by Quick setup, which creates policies in audit or test mode, or by a five-step custom setup. Roles include Insider Risk Management admins and Conditional Access or DLP administrators. Quick setup can take up to 72 hours, enabling can take 36 hours, and the capability is not available in US Government cloud programs.

admin-consent.title: Grant tenant-wide admin consent to an application - Microsoft Entra ID
admin-consent.notes: Admin consent in Microsoft Entra ID is an administrator's approval that lets an application use its requested permissions on behalf of the whole organization, so users are not prompted to consent when they sign in. The page warns it is sensitive because it can expose significant organizational data or highly privileged operations. It is needed when permissions should apply to all users, when an app uses application permissions (app roles) as a background service without a signed-in user, and when individual users should not consent themselves. Privileged Role Administrators can consent to any permission for any API; Cloud Application Administrators, AI Administrators and Application Administrators can do so except for Microsoft Graph application permissions; a custom role with the right permission also works. Consent can be granted in the portal from Enterprise applications (Permissions) or App registrations (API permissions), through a consent URL built from the client ID, or programmatically with Microsoft Graph PowerShell or the API using oauth2PermissionGrants for delegated and appRoleAssignedTo for application permissions.

advanced-connector-policies.title: Advanced connector policies - Power Platform - Microsoft Learn
advanced-connector-policies.notes: Advanced connector policies (ACP) are described as the next-generation way to govern connector usage in Power Platform. They replace the Business, Non-Business and Blocked classification of classic data policies with a strict allowlist that blocks all connectors by default, including newly added ones, and they build on the certified connector catalog. Policies can be set on a single environment or rolled out through environment groups, and blocking is enforced at design time as well as runtime, with action-level visibility so triggers or deprecated actions can be blocked. In mixed mode, which is the default, ACP runs alongside classic data policies and the most restrictive result applies; in ACP-only mode classic policies are ignored but not deleted. MCP servers are listed with other connectors and an entire server can be blocked, but control over individual MCP tools is not available yet. Certified connectors are supported; custom and HTTP connectors are not yet supported, and virtual connectors will not be. Each environment has at most one effective ACP, saving or publishing takes effect immediately and can break existing flows, and removing a group rule does not cascade to environments, which keep their last configuration.

advanced-planning-and-scheduling.title: Advanced planning and scheduling - Wikipedia
advanced-planning-and-scheduling.notes: Advanced planning and scheduling (APS) is a manufacturing management process that allocates raw materials and production capacity to meet demand, sometimes called advanced manufacturing. It suits situations where simpler planning cannot resolve complex trade-offs between competing priorities, since the number of possible production schedules grows roughly factorially with the number of products. APS plans and schedules at the same time, taking into account material availability, labor and plant capacity. Traditional manufacturing resource planning works through a stepwise procedure that is simple but cumbersome and adapts poorly to changes in demand, capacity or supply, and it usually plans materials and capacity separately, so plans can be infeasible. The article lists conditions where APS is typically applied: make-to-order production, capital-intensive plants with limited capacity, many products competing for the same capacity, products with many components or tasks, and frequent unpredictable schedule changes. It cautions that moving to APS has not always succeeded, which it attributes to the need to combine management philosophy with manufacturing practice, and it cites Stadtler and Kilger's work on supply chain management and advanced planning.

adx-studio.title: Microsoft acquires Adxstudio Inc., Web portal and application lifecycle management solutions provider
adx-studio.notes: In a post dated 28 September 2015, written by Bob Stutz, Corporate Vice President of Microsoft Dynamics CRM, Microsoft announced a definitive agreement to acquire key product and technology assets of Adxstudio Inc., together with team members and technology components. Adxstudio was a long-time Microsoft partner offering web portals, online engagement solutions and application lifecycle management for Dynamics CRM. Its portals were built natively on Dynamics CRM to extend sales and customer service processes online and worked with both online and on-premises customers, with integration into the Parature service and its knowledge management features. Pre-built solutions covered partner relationship management, technical support for high-tech and software companies, and online citizen engagement for the public sector. Microsoft justified the deal with Forrester research that web self-service had become the most popular channel customers use to find help, and said it would help customers and independent software vendors build CRM web engagement solutions on Microsoft technology. The post does not mention Power Pages or name the company's home country; those links are not stated on this page.

agent-feed.title: Supervise autonomous agents with agent feed - Microsoft Learn
agent-feed.notes: Agent feed is a task panel embedded in model-driven apps in Power Apps that gives people real-time visibility into, and control over, what autonomous agents do. It is meant for oversight of agent decisions, stepping in when needed and keeping agent work aligned with business rules and compliance standards. The feed shows a Needs attention list of tasks requiring human action, a Completed list that records who resolved each item for accountability and audit, an Insights panel with collaboration trends and filters by status or current record. Autonomous agents built in Copilot Studio that use the Power Apps MCP server create the tasks: an agent can ask for human help when blocked and wait asynchronously, or log completed work for passive oversight. The page positions it for areas such as customer communications, regulatory compliance, financial transactions, sensitive data and legal workflows, letting people shift from manual execution to supervision. The release plan lists public preview from 31 January 2026 with general availability not yet given, and was updated in August 2026. Microsoft notes that release plans stop being published from September 2026 in favor of an AI at Work roadmap.

agent-flows.title: Agent flows overview - Microsoft Copilot Studio
agent-flows.notes: Agent flows are automation workflows built in Microsoft Copilot Studio. Each has a trigger (instant, scheduled or event based, or started by an agent) and at least one action: AI capabilities such as generating text, processing documents or running a prompt, human-in-the-loop approvals or information requests, built-in tools for loops, branches, data operations and child flows, and Microsoft 365, third-party or custom connectors. Flows are deterministic, so the same input follows the same rule-based path, and they are designed and monitored in Copilot Studio's visual designer. A flow with the trigger When an agent calls the flow can be added as a tool to agents. Unlike Power Automate cloud flows, they are managed in Copilot Studio and consume Copilot Studio capacity (Copilot Credits) instead of Power Automate billing. Existing cloud flows in a solution can be converted by changing the plan to Copilot Studio; the conversion is one-way. When an environment has no credits, new runs are blocked while running ones finish, and runs started during a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot interaction or in test chat are not affected, whereas autonomous agent runs are charged. The page gives no numeric run or action limits.

agent-orchestrator.title: Orchestrate agent behavior with generative AI - Microsoft Copilot Studio
agent-orchestrator.notes: This Copilot Studio page describes generative orchestration, where an orchestrator uses generative AI to decide how an agent responds. On each message it selects one or more topics, tools, child or connected agents and knowledge sources, may use several in one turn, and then summarizes a single answer. Selection weighs, in order of importance, the descriptions of components, their names, and their input and output parameters; for topics the trigger shows that the agent chooses rather than listing phrases. If several components are chosen they run in sequence, and the agent first asks questions to collect missing inputs. The alternative is classic orchestration, which triggers the topic whose trigger phrases best match the query; new agents default to generative orchestration, and admins can turn it off for an environment. Best practices are simple, direct one-or-two-sentence descriptions, short unique names, relevant keywords, stating what a component cannot do, and avoiding overlapping descriptions, which make the pick unpredictable. Known limits include no closed-list or regex entities as parameters, limited conversation history, plain-text hyperlinks from knowledge sources and the Multiple Topics Matched system topic not being invoked. An activity map helps with testing.

agent-threads.title: Threads, Runs, and Messages in the Foundry Agent Service (classic) - Microsoft Learn
agent-threads.notes: In the classic Foundry Agent Service, a thread is a conversation session between an agent and a user. It stores messages and automatically truncates content to fit the model's context window, holds up to 100,000 messages, and persists until deleted; in the Standard agent setup threads live in the customer's Azure Cosmos DB account. Messages are individual pieces of communication, from the user or the agent, containing text or files such as images, kept as an ordered list. A run invokes the agent on a thread, using its instructions, tools and parameters, and may append response messages; statuses are queued, in_progress, requires_action, completed, failed, cancelled and expired. The recommended flow is to create an agent, create a thread once, append messages, run, monitor status, retrieve the response and delete unneeded threads. Guidance says to start a new thread for a new topic or a user wanting to start over, to give each user their own thread for isolation, and to move on from threads with thousands of messages because latency can grow. Poll run status from 500 ms with backoff, retry failures with exponential backoff, and plan storage costs and retention rules. The page warns that classic agents are deprecated and retire on 31 March 2027.

ai-builder-document-processing.title: Document processing model overview - AI Builder - Microsoft Learn
ai-builder-document-processing.notes: Document processing in AI Builder reads and saves information from standard documents such as invoices and tax documents, reviewing, extracting, organizing and storing the data automatically. A model must be trained and published before use. In training the maker defines which information to extract from example documents, and the page says only five documents are needed to get started, with little manual effort or data science expertise and accuracy tailored to the maker's own content. After publishing, the model can be called from cloud flows in Power Automate or from canvas apps in Power Apps. The page links to articles on creating, training and publishing such a model and to a Microsoft Learn training module on processing custom documents. It does not list supported file formats, size or page limits or usage quotas; those are referred to the availability-by-region and model types pages. The page's address uses the older form processing name, but it does not say that the feature was renamed.

ai-hallucination.title: Hallucination (artificial intelligence) - Wikipedia
ai-hallucination.notes: The article defines an AI hallucination as a response containing false or misleading information presented as fact, a loose analogy to human hallucination that some critics dislike because it anthropomorphizes software and prefer terms such as confabulation. Causes discussed include incomplete or unrepresentative training data, training to predict the next word so models guess when information is missing, creativity trade-offs, a model wrongly judging that it knows enough to answer (as in 2025 interpretability work), and evaluation that rewards guessing over admitting uncertainty. Examples include Meta's Galactica citing a fictitious paper in 2022, a 2023 court case where a lawyer submitted six fake precedents generated by ChatGPT and was fined 5,000 dollars, an Air Canada chatbot that invented a bereavement fare policy in 2024, and a study finding 47 percent of 115 ChatGPT-3.5 references fabricated. Mitigations include cleaner and augmented data, architecture changes, reinforcement learning, post-processing, neuro-symbolic approaches and guardrails, with trade-offs such as higher compute for scoring multiple answers. The term meant adding detail in 1980s computer vision and gained its current sense in the 2010s.

al-language.title: Programming in AL - Business Central - Microsoft Learn
al-language.notes: AL is the programming language of Dynamics 365 Business Central. It is used to retrieve, insert and modify records in the database, to control how application objects such as pages, reports and codeunits run, to move data between tables, combine data into reports, perform calculations such as totaling a sales order, steer application flow and create or modify objects. It also lets developers define business rules that keep stored data consistent with how customers do business. Code is attached to triggers on objects such as tables and table extensions, fields, pages and page extensions, reports and report extensions, data items, XMLports and queries, and runs when an action fires or an object is instantiated; local methods cannot be called from other objects. Variables are declared with the var keyword, and protected makes them accessible between tables and table extensions and between pages and page extensions. Microsoft advises placing logic in codeunits for cleaner design, reuse and security, since users usually cannot access sensitive tables such as General Ledger Entry directly but can run a codeunit that handles them; if code must sit on an object, put it close to what it operates on and centralize shared logic. The page defers extensions and tooling to other articles.

anti-corruption-layer.title: Anti-Corruption Layer Pattern - Azure Architecture Center - Microsoft Learn
anti-corruption-layer.notes: The anti-corruption layer pattern places a facade or adapter between two subsystems that do not share the same semantics, translating requests so that a dependency on a legacy or external system does not shape the design of the new application. Eric Evans introduced it in Domain-Driven Design. The problem it addresses is that, during gradual migration, new features still call legacy systems with convoluted schemas, obsolete APIs and outdated protocols, and integrating directly would force the new system to adopt those models. With the layer, each side keeps its own data model, and all translation logic lives in the layer, which can be a component inside the application or an independent service. The Azure example uses API Management for exposure, Azure Functions for translation and Azure Monitor for logging, with Service Bus, Event Grid or Event Hubs for asynchronous variants. Considerations are added latency, operational overhead, whether one or several layers are needed, whether it is permanent or retired after migration, data consistency, input validation at the trust boundary, correlation IDs for tracing and the risk of a single point of failure.

apache-parquet.title: Apache Parquet - Wikipedia
apache-parquet.notes: Apache Parquet is a free, open source, column-oriented file format for storing data, part of the Apache Hadoop ecosystem and usable with most processing frameworks. It stores the values of each column together, which allows compression and encoding suited to each column's type and faster queries because only the needed columns are read. Its design builds on the record shredding and assembly algorithm from Google's Dremel paper, so nested data structures are supported, and it was conceived as an improvement on Trevni. Version 1.0 arrived in 2013 and it has been a top-level Apache Software Foundation project since April 2015, under the Apache License 2.0. Supported codecs are Snappy, gzip, LZO, Brotli, Zstandard and LZ4, and encodings include dictionary encoding for columns with few unique values, bit packing, run-length encoding and a hybrid of the last two. Schema evolution is limited to adding columns and merging non-conflicting schemas. Tools such as Hive, Drill, Impala, Presto, Spark and pandas read it, and it is the base file format in cloud data lakes on Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage and Google Cloud Storage; Iceberg, Delta Lake and Hudi add a metadata layer on top. Compared with ORC and RCFile it offers better compression and read performance but slower writes.

applicant-tracking-system.title: Applicant tracking system - Wikipedia
applicant-tracking-system.notes: An applicant tracking system (ATS) is software that manages the recruitment and hiring process electronically. The article compares it to customer relationship management software built for recruiting. Listed functions are sourcing qualified candidates and posting jobs, parsing resumes and searching or filtering candidate databases, ranking and rating candidates, managing applicants and scheduling interviews, sending automated emails and reminders to candidates and hiring managers, and reporting and analytics. Because applications are filtered automatically, many candidates format their resumes with techniques similar to search engine optimization, tuning them for software rather than human readers. The article is brief and does not describe the history of ATS software in detail, and it does not list formal criticisms; its sources include a ResearchGate paper, a Coursera guide and a 2012 Wall Street Journal piece on resume screening.

application-access-policies.title: Role Based Access Control for Applications in Exchange Online - Microsoft Learn
application-access-policies.notes: This Microsoft Learn page covers Role Based Access Control for Applications in Exchange Online and treats Application Access Policies as the legacy mechanism that it replaces; it does not document how to create them. An application access policy constrains only the permissions consented in Microsoft Entra ID, whereas RBAC for Applications expresses authorization with a resource scope, and the two are additive. Organization-wide permissions belong in Entra ID and resource-scoped ones in RBAC for Applications. For migration, the scoping group of an existing policy can be reused: create a management scope with a MemberOfGroup filter using the group's distinguished name, create a service principal pointer with New-ServicePrincipal, assign a role such as Application Mail.Read with New-ManagementRoleAssignment and a custom resource scope, then remove the Entra consent and the old policy. Only direct group members count, not nested ones, and supported groups are Microsoft 365 groups, mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists. Limits include 10,000 applications per organization, a permission cache of 30 minutes to 2 hours, no AutoDiscover access, and support only for Microsoft Graph and EWS.

application-object-server.title: Configure batch-only and interactive-only AOS nodes in on-premises deployments - Microsoft Learn
application-object-server.notes: AOS stands for Application Object Server, the server component of Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations. This Microsoft Learn page does not describe AOS functions in depth; it covers how on-premises AOS nodes, which run on Azure Service Fabric, can be split by workload. Starting with application update 10.0.12 and platform update 36, two node types exist: BatchOnlyAOSNodeType runs batch jobs only, and InteractiveOnlyAOSNodeType serves interactive user sessions only. The traditional model, where one AOS node handles interactive sessions and also runs batch jobs, remains supported. New deployments define the node types in configtemplate.xml, and the original AOS node type is disabled when the split types are used. For existing deployments, nodes are removed and the new ones added, then Update Settings in Lifecycle Services triggers an environment refresh, which causes downtime. Minimum counts are two nodes of each type for sandbox environments and three of each type for production. The page supports the idea that interactive and batch workloads on AOS can be separated so that one does not starve the other, but it does not discuss integration traffic.

asset-administration-shell.title: What is the Asset Administration Shell from a technical view? - Plattform Industrie 4.0 / IDTA
asset-administration-shell.notes: This technical summary from Plattform Industrie 4.0's Task Force Secure Asset Administration Shell (April 2021) explains the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) as a generic term for a metamodel, its serializations in XML, JSON and RDF, instance data, file packages, server applications and APIs. The metamodel defines building blocks such as Asset, AAS, Submodel, SubmodelElementCollection and Property, and each asset, AAS and submodel has a globally unique identifier. Submodels group information about an asset; templates define structure while instances hold values, and they can sit inside an AAS or on separate servers. The goal is a standardized, machine-readable description of Industrie 4.0 assets so data can be exchanged and accessed consistently, combining static values with optional live values from devices. The AAS API gives read and write access and can run over HTTP/REST, OPC UA or MQTT, and a registry stores endpoints so shells can be found. The OPC UA companion specification I4AAS maps AAS data to OPC UA, and AAS data can be serialized as an OPC UA nodeset. Packages use the .AASX format with signatures for authenticity but no confidentiality by themselves. Security uses attribute-based access control, TLS and secure development per IEC 62443-4-1.

audience-targeting.title: Target navigation, news, files, links, and web parts to specific audiences - Microsoft Support
audience-targeting.notes: Audience targeting in SharePoint shows specific content to specific groups of people, prioritizing targeted items for those audiences so the most relevant content reaches them. It applies to navigation links, including hub and footer menus, to pages, files and folders in libraries such as Site Pages, to the Highlighted Content, News, Quick Links and Events web parts, and to Viva Connections dashboard cards, feed and dashboard web parts. Targeted content surfaces on the SharePoint start page, in news posts and in the mobile app. Audiences are Microsoft 365 groups and security groups, and Azure AD groups including dynamic groups, though dynamic groups are only partly supported for navigation. A navigation link can target up to 10 groups, and targeting a parent link also applies to its sub-links. The site owner must first enable audience targeting for site navigation and, once per library, for that library; after that, editors can set audiences. Editors continue to see all links while editing. Page changes and audience settings take effect only after publishing or republishing, and newly created or changed groups can take time before targeting applies. Web parts without targeting remain visible to everyone.

authentication-strength.title: Overview of Conditional Access Authentication Strengths - Microsoft Entra ID
authentication-strength.notes: An authentication strength is a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access control that defines which combinations of authentication methods a user may use to reach a resource. A sensitive resource can require phishing-resistant methods while a less sensitive one accepts weaker MFA. It builds on the tenant's authentication methods policy, which sets available methods, and is applied through a Conditional Access policy with the Require authentication strength grant control. Microsoft ships three built-in strengths that cannot be edited: MFA, Passwordless MFA and Phishing-resistant MFA. FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business or platform credentials and multifactor certificate-based authentication satisfy all three; Microsoft Authenticator phone sign-in satisfies MFA and passwordless; Temporary Access Pass and password plus a second factor satisfy MFA only. Administrators can create custom strengths for exact method combinations.

authority-bias.title: Authority bias - Wikipedia
authority-bias.notes: Authority bias is the tendency to regard an authority figure's opinion as more accurate regardless of its content, and to be more influenced by and more likely to obey it. The article classes it as a social or collective cognitive bias and gives reasons such as perceived legitimacy, socialization in hierarchies from childhood, evolutionary advantages of deferring to those controlling resources and its use as a decision shortcut that becomes a problem when blind. Key studies include Milgram's 1963 obedience research, where obedience fell from 65 percent to 20 percent when an ordinary person in plain clothes gave the instructions, Bickman's 1974 study in which passers-by were about twice as likely to comply with someone dressed as a security guard as with someone dressed as a milkman, and the Hofling hospital study in which 21 of 22 nurses were willing to give a potentially fatal dose on a doctor's request. Effects appear in marketing, medicine through the expert halo effect, wrongful convictions based on forensic testimony and organizations through the HIPPO effect, deference to the highest-paid person's opinion. The article notes that research is largely correlational, that cues such as uniforms are easy to fake and that confirmation bias can compound the effect.

automated-machine-learning.title: What is automated ML? AutoML - Azure Machine Learning - Microsoft Learn
automated-machine-learning.notes: Automated machine learning (AutoML) automates the time-consuming, iterative work of model development so data scientists, analysts and developers can build models at scale while keeping quality. In Azure Machine Learning it is based on a Microsoft Research breakthrough. During training, many pipelines run in parallel with different algorithms and parameters; each iteration yields a model with a score on the target metric, and the process stops at the exit criteria defined for the experiment. The user identifies the problem, chooses code-first (SDK v2 or CLI v2) or the no-code studio, supplies labeled data, sets iterations, featurization and metrics, submits the job and reviews results, which include a serialized pickle model with its preprocessing and feature importance. Supported tasks are classification, regression, time-series forecasting, computer vision (image classification, object detection, instance segmentation) and natural language processing with BERT models in 104 languages. Featurization such as normalization and missing-data handling is automatic and becomes part of the model. Ensembles by voting or stacking are enabled by default, selected with the Caruana algorithm.
